gloss: summer fatigue; exhaustion from the summer heat

definitions.gloss: summer fatigue; exhaustion from the summer heat
definitions.explanation: physical and mental tiredness caused by prolonged exposure to hot, humid summer weather

examples.japanese: {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食欲|しょくよく}→食欲：03249_shokuyoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: I have no appetite because of summer fatigue.

examples.japanese: ⟦{九月|くがつ}→九月：00646_kugatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}→出る：00513_deru⟧やすい。
examples.english: Summer fatigue tends to set in once September arrives.

examples.japanese: {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦しっかり→しっかり：01272_shikkari⟧⟦{睡眠|すいみん}→睡眠：03359_suimin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦{栄養|えいよう}→栄養：01882_eiyou⟧⟦バランス→バランス：03870_baransu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧よい⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{心|こころ}がけよう→心がける：10015_kokorogakeru⟧。
examples.english: To prevent summer fatigue, make sure to get enough sleep and eat a well-balanced diet.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧ (summer) + ⟦{疲|つか}れ→疲れ：03518_tsukare⟧ (fatigue). Refers to the accumulated tiredness from enduring Japan's hot and humid summers, often manifesting as loss of appetite, lethargy, and weakened immunity. Symptoms often peak in late August to September.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: for summer fatigue to set in
- {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧: to prevent summer fatigue
- {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{解消|かいしょう}する→解消する：21324_kaishousuru⟧: to recover from summer fatigue
- {夏疲|なつづか}れ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{効|き}く→効く：01932_kiku⟧: effective against summer fatigue

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{夏|なつ}バテ→夏バテ：15545_natsubate⟧: summer lethargy — very similar; more colloquial and more commonly used
- ⟦{疲労|ひろう}→疲労：13603_hirou⟧: fatigue — general term for tiredness, not season-specific
- ⟦{熱中症|ねっちゅうしょう}→熱中症：08330_necchuushou⟧: heatstroke — a more acute, dangerous condition from heat exposure

NOTE: ⟦{夏|なつ}バテ→夏バテ：15545_natsubate⟧ is the more common everyday term for the same concept. {夏疲|なつづか}れ is slightly more literary but widely understood.
